title: Ὄνος καὶ ἡμίονος ⟨ἐξ ἴσου ἐμπεφορτισμένοι⟩
titleEn: The Donkey and the Mule Loaded Equally
part: The Donkey and the Mule Loaded Equally (Chambry 272 · Perry 263)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 272 (= Perry 263). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« », ⟨ ⟩ for editorial supplements). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ὄνος καὶ ἡμίονος ἐν ταὐτῷ ἐβάδιζον.
sentences.tr: Onos kai hēmionos en tautōi ebadizon.
sentences.l: A donkey and a mule were walking in the same place.
sentences.i: A donkey and a mule were walking along together.
sentences.n: ταὐτῷ is crasis, τῷ αὐτῷ run together into one word; the mark over the upsilon is the coronis, which looks exactly like a smooth breathing. ἐν ταὐτῷ, 'in the same place', is the ordinary way of saying 'in company'. Chambry supplies the second half of the title, ⟨ἐξ ἴσου ἐμπεφορτισμένοι⟩, 'loaded equally', in his angle brackets.

sentences.t: Καὶ δὴ ὁ ὄνος ὁρῶν τοὺς ἀμφοῖν γόμους ἴσους ὄντας ἠγανάκτει καὶ ἐσχετλίαζεν, εἴγε διπλασίονος τροφῆς ἠξιωμένη ἡ ἡμίονος οὐδὲν περιττότερον βαστάζει.
sentences.tr: Kai dē ho onos horōn tous amphoin gomous isous ontas ēganaktei kai eschetliazen, eige diplasionos trophēs ēxiōmenē hē hēmionos ouden perittoteron bastazei.
sentences.l: And indeed the donkey, seeing the loads of the two of them to be equal, was growing indignant and complaining bitterly, if indeed the mule, thought worthy of double fodder, carries nothing more.
sentences.i: And so the donkey, seeing that the loads of the pair were equal, grew indignant and complained bitterly that the mule, allowed a double ration, was carrying nothing extra.
sentences.n: ἀμφοῖν is a genitive dual — the old two-of-them form, which Greek keeps for natural pairs. εἴγε, 'if indeed', gives the ground of the grievance rather than a real condition. ἡ ἡμίονος is feminine, as her own speech at the end confirms; the mule of these fables is regularly a she-mule. βαστάζει is a present indicative kept inside a past narrative, which brings the complaint into the donkey's own words. A printing note: the page has no omicron in περιττότερον — a blank exactly one letter wide sits where it should be, confirmed at 600 dpi. It is a failed sort, not a variant reading, so the word is given whole here; this is the one place in the fable where the text is not the literal ink.

sentences.t: Μικρὸν δὲ αὐτῶν τῆς ὁδοῦ προϊόντων, ὁ ὀνηλάτης ὁρῶν τὸν ὄνον ἀντέχειν μὴ δυνάμενον, ἀφελόμενος αὐτοῦ τὸ φορτίον τῇ ἡμιόνῳ ἐπέθηκεν.
sentences.tr: Mikron de autōn tēs hodou proiontōn, ho onēlatēs horōn ton onon antechein mē dynamenon, aphelomenos autou to phortion tēi hēmionōi epethēken.
sentences.l: And as they advanced a little of the road, the donkey-driver, seeing the donkey not able to hold out, having taken his load from him, set it upon the mule.
sentences.i: When they had gone a little way along the road, the driver saw that the donkey could not hold out, took the load off him and set it on the mule.
sentences.n: A genitive absolute, αὐτῶν προϊόντων, with τῆς ὁδοῦ a partitive genitive: they advance 'a little of the road'. ἀφαιρέομαι in the middle is to take a thing away from someone for oneself, and takes the genitive of the person, αὐτοῦ. That the transfer is by instalments only becomes clear in the next sentence, where the driver goes on shifting until nothing is left.

sentences.t: Ἔτι δὲ αὐτῶν πόρρω προβαινόντων, ὁρῶν ἔτι μᾶλλον ἀποκάμνοντα, πάλιν ἀπὸ τοῦ γόμου μετετίθει, μέχρι τὰ πάντα λαβὼν καὶ ἀφελόμενος ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ τῇ ἡμιόνῳ ἐπέθηκε.
sentences.tr: Eti de autōn porrō probainontōn, horōn eti mallon apokamnonta, palin apo tou gomou metetithei, mechri ta panta labōn kai aphelomenos ap’ autou tēi hēmionōi epethēke.
sentences.l: And as they went on still further, seeing him flagging yet more, again he kept shifting some of the load across, until, having taken it all and removed it from him, he set it upon the mule.
sentences.i: And as they went further still, seeing him tiring more and more, he shifted more of the load across again, until he had taken the whole of it off him and set it on the mule.
sentences.n: μετατίθημι in the active is simply to move a thing from one place to another; the imperfect μετετίθει says he did it again and again. (The same verb in the middle means to shift one's own ground, and so to change one's mind — a different word in effect.) ἀποκάμνω is to tire to the point of giving up, not merely to be weary.

sentences.t: Καὶ τότε ἐκείνη ἀποβλέψασα εἰς τὸν ὄνον εἶπεν· « Ὦ οὗτος, ἆρά σοι οὐ δοκῶ δικαίως τῆς διπλῆς τροφῆς ἀξιωθῆναι ; »
sentences.tr: Kai tote ekeinē apoblepsasa eis ton onon eipen· « Ō houtos, ara soi ou dokō dikaiōs tēs diplēs trophēs axiōthēnai ; »
sentences.l: And then she, having looked across at the donkey, said: « You there, do I not seem to you to have been rightly thought worthy of the double ration? »
sentences.n: ἆρα … οὐ is the question that expects agreement: 'surely I do?' δοκῶ is personal — Greek says 'I seem to have been thought worthy' where English would as readily say 'does it not seem'. ἀξιωθῆναι picks up ἠξιωμένη from the donkey's own complaint and turns it back on him.

sentences.t: Ἀτὰρ οὖν καὶ ἡμᾶς προσήκει μὴ ἀπὸ τῆς ἀρχῆς, ἀλλ’ ἀπὸ τοῦ τέλους τὴν ἑκάστου δοκιμάζειν διάθεσιν.
sentences.tr: Atar oun kai hēmas prosēkei mē apo tēs archēs, all’ apo tou telous tēn hekastou dokimazein diathesin.
sentences.l: So then it befits us too to judge each man's disposition not from the beginning but from the end.
sentences.n: The closing formula is the familiar Ἀτὰρ οὖν καὶ ἡμᾶς, 'so then we too', in which the fable turns and takes the reader in; here it is προσήκει, 'it is fitting', that stands where δεῖ or χρή usually does. δοκιμάζω is to put a thing to the test and so pass judgement on it — the word used of assaying metal. διάθεσις is the settled condition a person is in, hence his quality or worth.
